task: Exercise staged nominal Map key lowering through a Margo project.
observation: After rebuilding the compiler, the same Margo probe reused previously generated Rust for an unchanged Moss source file, so its first native failure still reflected the prior lowering. Cleaning only the probe project forced regeneration and exposed the current result.
impact: A compiler implementation change can appear ineffective in an incremental package probe unless its generated Rust cache is invalidated; this delayed diagnosis of the empty Map declaration.
evidence: tmp/phase25-i-map-staging/tmp/phase25-map-key-probe/build/debug/Provider.rs: pre-clean output retained untyped Map local
src/moss.cpp: staged Map local type and object-view lowering
tests/tooling/check_phase25_conformance.py: activated Gate 10 passed after clean rebuild

resolution.summary: Used margo clean on the isolated probe before native validation. The activated G2 conformance suite passed 11/11 gates on the rebuilt compiler; cache-key hardening remains separate from this staging change.
